steps.note: A — the frame as it opens, untouched
B — census of everything the props kit actually put in the scene
=== GAP 1 RE-CHECK: are the props planted? Measured, not eyeballed. ===
G1a — geometry: world AABB base of every prop instance vs the ground raycast under it
G1b — the contact-pool mesh itself
G1c — A/B: the same frame with the contact pools hidden and shown, at a low gameplay angle
G1d — same A/B on open grass where the trees stand
G1e — sun shadow off, so only the contact pools are left doing the grounding
G1f — grazing angle at eye height: any prop base that floats shows sky/grass under it here
=== GAP 2 RE-CHECK: is the see-through a clean ghost or still a screen door? ===
G2a — walk under the trees with the lens in tight; whatever covers the boy should ghost
G2b — crawl the lens all the way in (min zoom): the old near-melt dither lived here
G2c — hand the see-through to the props kit instead of the camera and look again
=== NEW HUNTING ===
C — every edge, looking OUT of the vale, then back IN
D — the inhabited middle
E — repetition: five places, identical camera. One place copied, or five places?
F — z-fighting / decals: steep top-down on the lane where the path meets the grass
G — motion: camera and hero dead still for seven seconds. Anything frozen here is a statue.
H — dusk and night: do the lanterns light, does the set dressing survive?
NaN / geometry health: anything the build computed as NaN while we drove it
I — what the triangles are spent on, and the closing numbers
